standard_prerequisites.name: The N-2 criterion: a discrete valuation ring is Nagata exactly when it is N-2
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces Nagata-ness of A to finiteness of integral closures in purely inseparable extensions.

standard_prerequisites.name: The tensor product of a separable and a purely inseparable extension is a field
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the field in which the auxiliary integral closure B_1 is taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful flatness of A -> B and descent of finiteness of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Carries finiteness from B tensor_A A_1 over B down to A_1 over A.

core_obligations: Recall that a discrete valuation ring is Nagata if and only if it is N-2, and reduce to showing that for a finite purely inseparable extension K_1/K the integral closure A_1 of A in K_1 is finite over A (proof lines 35674-35677).
Use that L/K is separable and K_1/K is purely inseparable to conclude that L tensor_K K_1 is a field (proof lines 35678-35681).
Let B_1 be the integral closure of B in L tensor_K K_1; since B is Nagata, B_1 is finite over B (proof lines 35682-35683).
Since B tensor_A A_1 is contained in B_1 and B is Noetherian, conclude that B tensor_A A_1 is finite over B (proof lines 35683-35685).
Use faithful flatness of A -> B and the descent lemma for module properties to conclude that A_1 is finite over A, hence that A is Nagata (proof lines 35686-35687).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings and asserts that if B is Nagata and the extension L/K of fraction fields is separable, then A is Nagata (source lines 35666-35671). The proof first recalls the criterion that a discrete valuation ring is Nagata exactly when it is N-2, so it suffices to show that for a finite purely inseparable extension K_1/K the integral closure A_1 of A in K_1 is finite over A (proof lines 35674-35677). The substantive step is the field-theoretic observation: since L/K is separable and K_1/K is purely inseparable, the algebra L tensor_K K_1 is a field, by the reducedness and radicial-integrality lemmas (proof lines 35678-35681). Letting B_1 be the integral closure of B in that field, Nagata-ness of B makes B_1 finite over B; since B tensor_A A_1 is contained in B_1 and B is Noetherian, that subring is finite over B (proof lines 35682-35685). The final step is descent: because A -> B is faithfully flat, finiteness of B tensor_A A_1 over B implies finiteness of A_1 over A, by the descent lemma for properties of modules (proof lines 35685-35687). The non-routine content is the field-theoretic identification of the base change as a field, which is what allows Nagata-ness of B to be tested there, together with the faithful flat descent at the end.
